The manager package provides a set of geochemical visualization functions for evaluating groundwater and surface water chemistry.

Currently supported plots include:

Piper diagrams
Schoeller diagrams
Stiff diagrams

These plots share a common data preparation workflow that ensures consistent analyte handling, unit standardization, and conversion to milliequivalents per liter (meq/L).

```{r, echo = FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(manager)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.path = "figures/geochemical-"
)
```

```{r example-dataset}
data("gw_data")
dplyr::glimpse(gw_data)
```
Geochemical Plot Workflow
All geochemical plotting functions follow the same processing pipeline.

1. Resolve analyte aliases to canonical analytes.
2. Validate analyte-unit consistency.
3. Standardize analytical units.
4. Convert concentrations to milliequivalents per liter (meq/L).
5. Transform data into plot-specific coordinates.
6. Render visualization.

This workflow allows plotting functions to accept either canonical analyte names or approved analyte aliases while maintaining consistent chemistry calculations.

Piper Diagram
A Piper diagram is commonly used to classify water types and evaluate hydrochemical facies.

The plot is generated directly from the analytical data.
```{r, piper, fig.height=6, fig.width=9, results='hide', warning=FALSE}
gw_data %>%
  piper_plot()
```
Schoeller Diagram
A Schoeller diagram displays major ion concentrations on a logarithmic scale and is useful for:

Comparing groundwater chemistry between wells
Evaluating temporal trends
Identifying mixing relationships
Screening for anomalous chemistry
```{r schoeller, fig.height=6, fig.width=9, results='hide', warning=FALSE}
gw_data %>%
  schoeller_plot()
```

```{r stiff, eval=FALSE, fig.height=6, fig.width=9, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE, results='hide'}
gw_data %>%
  filter(location_id == "MW-1") %>%
  stiff_plot(., total_dissolved_solids = "Total Dissolved Solids")
```
